title: Material Management Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) FMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
18.     MOS 8862, Material Management Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) FMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Material Management Officers analyze, review, and seek to
improve operations and project management, business modeling for decision
making, and inventory management systems as they relate to Marine Corps
logistic functions. Provide a comprehensive background in quantitative
problem-solving methods, operations management, behavioral and management
science, economic analysis, and financial management, as applicable to
logistic systems and processes in the Marine Corps.

       b.   Prerequisites.   None.




                                         1-359                       Enclosure (1)
 1147                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



    c. Requirements. Complete the Material Logistics Support Management
Curriculum Number 827 at Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, CA, or
equivalent postgraduate degree at a comparable accredited institution.

       d.   Duties

            (1) Monitors the status of logistic management information.

        (2) Provides expertise on the principal means of accumulating,
transmitting, processing, storing, and applying such information to
management systems.

        (3) Coordinates the design and control of logistic management
information systems with present technological capabilities.

        (4) Applies state-of-the-art logistics concepts, tools, and
methodologies from public management and business to solve relevant supply
chain management problems and to achieve cost-effective operational
readiness.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Management Analysts 13-1111.

            (2) Logisticians 13-1081.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

Analyze information obtained from management to conceptualize and define operational problems.

Provide a comprehensive background in quantitative problem-solving methods, operations management, behavioral and management science, economic analysis, and financial management, as applicable to logistic systems and processes in the Marine Corps.
Maintain records of daily activities, personnel reports, ship positions and movements, ports of call, weather and sea conditions, pollution control efforts, or cargo or passenger status.
d. Duties (1) Monitors the status of logistic management information.
Analyze information obtained from management to conceptualize and define operational problems.
(2) Provides expertise on the principal means of accumulating, transmitting, processing, storing, and applying such information to management systems.
Provide logistics technology or information for effective and efficient support of product, equipment, or system manufacturing or service.
(3) Coordinates the design and control of logistic management information systems with present technological capabilities.
Apply logistics modeling techniques to address issues, such as operational process improvement or facility design or layout.

(4) Applies state-of-the-art logistics concepts, tools, and methodologies from public management and business to solve relevant supply chain management problems and to achieve cost-effective operational readiness.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
